beats.text: A mechanical mouse learned its way through a maze.
beats.note: Claude Shannon built Theseus, which finds its way to the goal and remembers the path.
Relays beneath the maze calculated its position and remembered successful and unsuccessful paths.
When its whiskers touched a wall, a relay flipped from on to off, recording a wall on that side.

beats.text: The circuitry was wired on the living room floor.
beats.note: Parts of the maze were machined at Bell Labs, but the circuitry was built at home.

beats.text: The MIT Museum holds the original maze.
One of the first learning machines was a mouse running on telephone relays.

beats.line: AI started with a mouse and a telephone exchange.
